title: [MEDIUM] GitLenient URL prefix match lacks path-segment boundary
description:
**File:** [`crates/solid-pod-rs/src/auth/nip98.rs`](https://github.com/DreamLab-AI/solid-pod-rs/blob/fix/nip98-empty-body/blob/fix/crates/solid-pod-rs/src/auth/nip98.rs#L168-L395) (lines 168, 395)
**Project:** solid-pod-empty-body
**Severity:** MEDIUM  •  **Confidence:** medium  •  **Slug:** `other-scope-boundary`

## Owners

**Suggested assignee:** `github@xrsystems.uk` _(via last-committer)_

## Finding

Under MatchPolicy::GitLenient the URL binding is accepted when `e.starts_with(t)` (line 168), where `t` is the normalized token URL (trailing slash trimmed) and `e` the normalized request URL. This is a raw string prefix test with no path-separator boundary. A token scoped to `https://pod.example/alice/repo` therefore also satisfies the scope check for sibling paths that merely share a character prefix, e.g. `https://pod.example/alice/repo-backup/...` or `https://pod.example/alice/repository/...`, not just true sub-paths like `…/repo/info/refs`. normalize_url (line 395-397) only trims trailing slashes, so the trimmed base has no trailing `/` to force a boundary. The signing pubkey is still cryptographically verified, so this is a scope-binding (defence-in-depth) weakening rather than a full auth bypass: the git bridge's single static token is meant to cover exactly one repo's smart-protocol sub-paths, but it will also authenticate requests to adjacent repo paths sharing the prefix. The existing test only covers a different top-level user (bob vs alice) and does not exercise the sibling-prefix case.

## Recommendation

Require a true path boundary for the lenient case, e.g. accept only when `e == t || e.starts_with(&format!("{t}/"))`, so `…/repo` matches `…/repo/...` but not `…/repo-backup`.
